scope: One researcher-clarified historical task 728 paired with unchanged current task 733; four dependent development conditions, not four independent tasks

usage.note: Conservative client accounting, not an invoice. Declared tool units are not yuan or measured execution costs.

interpretation: No final-answer error or cache-route choice was observed in this one adapted sufficient-history control.
Availability and the two declared prices did not change the observed SQL-then-answer route. Both cache prices were below the SQL price of 10; no price-order reversal was tested.
No prior task contract was elicited. This batch does not establish either presence or absence of C-type requirement reinterpretation.
No cache read occurred, so downstream effects of consuming cached rows were not tested by these trajectories.
Classical grouped-view selection already covers the positive control. These observations do not demonstrate a novel method or superiority over strong checks plus recomputation.

next_decision.stage: Development feasibility control complete; phenomenon and method gap remain unproven
next_decision.recommendation: Retain this no-error/no-reuse result. Do not enlarge or retune this same task merely to obtain errors. Before another paid batch, inspect the existing interface and specify a task-based, outcome-independent sample and strong-baseline gap.
next_decision.forced_cache_arm: If proposed later, label as a separate diagnostic intervention, not evidence that the ordinary agent spontaneously chose cache reuse.
